title: Fold a car's flip key shut in the hands: release button held in, blade swung home until it latches
instruction: Fold the car key shut and put it back in the tray.
context: A car's flip key folds shut only while its release button is held in, and it latches only if the blade is swung all the way home before the button is let out; let go short of the catch and the spring flicks it open again. Most cars sold in the last fifteen years by Kia, Hyundai, Volkswagen, Ford and others come with such a key, and owners fold it every time they put it away. The maker says how: 'To fold the key, fold the key manually while pressing the release button. Do not fold the key without pressing the release button. This may damage the key.' (Kia owner's manual, Key operations). Done in the hands, as people do it, a robot needs both: one hand holds the fob with a pad on the button while the other swings the blade half a turn home, and the fob must change hands, the pushing hand closing over the folded blade, before the button is let out so that the catch can drop. Then the key goes back in its tray.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x away from the arms, y to the left); heights over the bench top. Key tray: a round ceramic plate, Fiesta 7 1/4 in salad plate in Turquoise glaze (about 184 mm across, floor about 150 mm, 20 mm high (a)), its middle at x 28, y 0 (a mark on the bench). Car key: Kia folding key (Kia Soul, 4-button remote): black fob 70 x 34 x 16 mm, 35 g (a), steel blade 60 x 9 x 2.5 mm (a) latched OPEN, lying flat in the tray, buttons up, its open length centred on the tray. Varies by seed: the key's turn about the vertical through the tray's middle, 115 to 200 degrees (fob's long axis, pin end, from +x towards +y); seed 0 gives 169.1 degrees; --seed 0 under the harness gives the trial seed 1415158438, 174.9 degrees. Both arms start in their ready pose. (a): assumed, to be measured on the bought parts (README, bench test).
scoring: The end state counts, except 'picked up', 'swung home in the hands' and 'left the bench', which hold over the whole trial and are checked from the trial video. 1.0: the blade folded and latched (on the bench: a 2 N pull on its tip, button not pressed, leaves it in), swung home in the hands (when the blade reached its folded end, the key's middle was 2 cm or more over where it lay at the start), the key resting in the tray, inside the floor's edge, at rest, both grippers 3 cm or more from it. 0.5: the same with the key anywhere else on the bench. 0.25: folded and latched, but swung home with the key lying in the tray or on the bench; or the key picked up and its blade turned 90 degrees or more towards folded at some moment, the end state being neither of the above (blade held part-folded, or the folded key still held). 0: the blade open at the end; or any part of the key 2 cm or more under the bench top at any moment (it fell); or less than the above. A blade pushed without the button does not move, as on the real key.
reset_notes: About 1 minute: fold the blade out with the button until it latches open; set the tray on its mark on the bench (its middle within 5 mm); lay the key in it buttons up at the seed's turn, its open length centred; check with a photo from above against the seed's start picture (the key's turn within 5 degrees, its middle within 5 mm of the tray's middle). Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at true size. The blade's spring (0.02 to 0.05 N m, assumed) is a torque computed each step. The pawl is the blade hinge's end stops, freed while the button is in 0.9 mm or more; its strength is not modelled (the stops hold any load). Blade and button move with the inertia of 50 g and 20 g (real about 9 g and 1 g), their extra weight carried by a push. Button force 2 to 4 N, assumed. Not modelled: the remote's electronics and the key ring.
